dec_1.title: Magic Word: if
dec_1.prompt: The word "if" in Python is used to...
dec_1.explanation: if is like asking: "IF this is true, do that". For example: IF it's raining, take an umbrella! ☔
options: Ask a question and decide what to do

dec_2.title: else is Mandatory
dec_2.prompt: When we use if, we are required to use else as well.
dec_2.explanation: Not always! else is optional. You only use it when you want something to happen if the condition is false. Like having a plan B! 🅱️

dec_3.title: Comparing Values
dec_3.prompt: Which symbol do we use to check if two values are EQUAL?
dec_3.explanation: Two equals (==) to compare! One equal (=) assigns values. Two equals (==) asks: "Are they equal?" ⚖️

dec_4.title: Is an Adult?
dec_4.prompt: Complete the code to show "Maior de idade" if age is 18 or older:
dec_4.explanation: We use if to check: IF age >= 18, show message! The >= sign means "greater than or equal to". 📊

dec_5.title: Even or Odd?
dec_5.prompt: Complete the code to check if the number is even:
dec_5.explanation: % gives remainder of division. If numero % 2 == 0, the remainder is 0, so it is even! 🎲

cond_parsons_rain.title: Rainy Day
cond_parsons_rain.prompt: Build the logic: If it is raining, take an umbrella. Else, wear sunglasses.
cond_parsons_rain.explanation: Computer checks the condition in `if`. If true, runs the first block. If not, jumps to `else`!

dec_6.title: Many Options
dec_6.prompt: Use `elif` to check if grade is 8:
dec_6.explanation: When we have more than one option, we use elif (means "else if"). Like saying: "If not the first, check this one..." 🤔

cond_and_1.title: Two Conditions Together
cond_and_1.prompt: Which word do we use to check if BOTH conditions are true?
cond_and_1.explanation: and means both must be true! if idade >= 18 and tem_ingresso: checks if adult AND has ticket. 🎫

cond_or_1.title: One or the Other
cond_or_1.prompt: Complete to check if it is Saturday OR Sunday:
cond_or_1.explanation: or means either one! If ONE condition is true, it enters the if. 🌴

cond_not_1.title: Negating with not
cond_not_1.prompt: The "not" operator inverts a condition. If something is True, not turns it into False.
cond_not_1.explanation: not flips everything! not True = False, not False = True. Like saying "It is NOT true that..." 🔄

cond_in_1.title: Check if in List
cond_in_1.prompt: How do we check if "banana" is in the fruit list?
cond_in_1.explanation: in checks if something is inside a list or string! "banana" in frutas returns True if banana is in the list. 🍌

cond_in_2.title: Checking Letter
cond_in_2.prompt: Complete to check if the letter "a" is in the word:
cond_in_2.explanation: in works with text too! "a" in "banana" is True because banana contains the letter a! 🔤

dec_7.title: Not Equal Symbol
dec_7.prompt: The != symbol means "not equal" in Python.
dec_7.explanation: That's right! The exclamation mark ! with = means "not equal"! 3 != 4 is True! ≠

turtle_colors.title: Conditional Colors
turtle_colors.prompt: Complete the code to draw 4 lines: if the number is even, use blue; if odd, use red.
turtle_colors.explanation: Use if/else to pick colors! If i is even (i % 2 == 0), use blue. Else, use red! 🎨

dec_8.title: Traffic Light
dec_8.prompt: Complete with elif for the yellow light:
dec_8.explanation: elif tests another condition if the first fails! "If green, go. ELSE IF yellow, caution!". 🚦

dec_9.title: Roller Coaster
dec_9.prompt: To ride the coaster, need height > 1.20 AND age >= 10:
dec_9.explanation: When we need TWO things at the same time, we use "and"! Height ok AND Age ok = Fun! 🎢

dec_10.title: Less Than
dec_10.explanation: Yes! < means "less than". 5 is less than 10, so answer is True! ✅

dec_11.title: If NOT True
dec_11.prompt: What does the code `if not chovendo:` do?
dec_11.explanation: `not` inverts condition! If `chovendo` is False (not raining), `not chovendo` becomes True and code runs! ☀️
options: Runs if it is NOT raining

dec_12.title: Weekend
dec_12.prompt: Which code correctly checks if it is Saturday OR Sunday?
dec_12.explanation: We use `or`! Computer checks: Is it Saturday? OR Is it Sunday? If either is true, you can rest! 🎮

dec_13.title: Third Option
dec_13.prompt: If not 1 or 2, check if it is 3 using elif:
dec_13.explanation: elif saves the day! Checks the next option if previous ones failed. "If not 1 nor 2... what about 3?" 🤔

dec_14.title: Sunny Day
dec_14.prompt: If it is NOT raining, I go to the beach. Which code does this?
dec_14.explanation: `not` flips logic! If `chovendo` is False, `not chovendo` becomes True and we hit the beach! 🏖️

dec_15.title: In the Middle
dec_15.prompt: Check if the number is greater than 10 AND less than 20:
dec_15.explanation: We use `and` when we want TWO things to be true at the same time. Greater than 10 AND less than 20! 🤝

dec_16.title: Item in Backpack
dec_16.prompt: Check if "lanterna" is in your backpack:
dec_16.explanation: `in` is like a detective! Searches inside the list and tells you if it found what you wanted. 🔦

boss_battle_4.title: The Logic Sphinx
boss_battle_4.prompt: The Sphinx asks: If vida = 100 and vida > 50, show "Você está bem!". Else, show "Cuidado!".
boss_battle_4.explanation: The Sphinx tests your logic! Use if and else to choose what to display! 🦁
